mainTopic: Does a קנס become ordinary money after trial? רבה and אביי debate the קרבן שבועה, inheritance, and the fine of אונס and מפתה, and רב יוסף answers from ״וְנָתַן״.
overview: רבה holds that once a man has stood trial for a קנס, the payment counts as regular money. אביי challenges him from a ברייתא about a false oath on money owed. The רישא of that ברייתא includes כפל, which exists only after trial, so the סיפא, where רבי שמעון exempts, must also be after trial. רבה answers that the רישא follows the רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי שמעון. He agrees that ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ exempts from a קרבן שבועה, and says that calling the fine ממון only means the father's sons can inherit it. אביי objects that רבי שמעון gives uncollected payments to the daughter, not to the brothers. After twenty-two years רב יוסף answered from ״וְנָתַן״: the father owns the fine of the girl only once it is given, so רבה's inheritance rule covers other fines. The גמרא tests this reading against the slave verse (״יִתֵּן״) and against the ברייתא's use of ״וְכִחֵשׁ״. The גמרא answers that ״יִתֵּן״ differs from ״וְנָתַן״. רבא answers the ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ challenge, and רב נחמן בר יצחק answers a follow-up challenge about the word קנס. A final challenge from רבי שמעון's words in the משנה is answered: he was arguing with the רבנן on their own terms, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't the case one where he already stood trial?
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests that the ברייתא's case, where רבי שמעון exempts, is after trial. If so, it contradicts רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about a case where he already stood trial?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his challenge. He suggests that the case in the ברייתא, where רבי שמעון treats the fine as a fine, happened after the man stood trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that after trial, a קנס becomes ordinary money. If רבי שמעון still treats it as a fine even after trial, רבה's view is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: "Isn't it...?" A way of suggesting a reading in order to prove a point
Stood trial: the court already found him liable
A fine: a payment set by the Torah, not tied to actual damage

phrases.english: What, is it not where he has stood trial?!
phrases.notes: This is about the last part of the ברייתא, where רבי שמעון exempts the man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's challenge from the ברייתא, which began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that a קנס becomes ordinary money once he has stood trial.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי שמעון still exempts after trial, then a fine stays a fine even after trial.

steps.title: No, he had not yet stood trial
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא's case is before trial.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about a case where he had not stood trial.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes away the challenge. He says the case in the ברייתא is before any trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before trial, everyone agrees a קנס is still a fine. So רבי שמעון's exemption there does not touch רבה's rule about after trial.

keyTerms.meaning: No: the start of a rejecting answer

phrases.english: No, where he has not stood trial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the case as a different situation (before trial).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about after trial, so it contradicts רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about before trial, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The first part is after trial, so the later part must be too
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that since the רישא is after trial, the סיפא should be after trial as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the first part is talking about after trial, the later part is also talking about after trial.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back. He claims the first part of the same ברייתא is clearly about after trial, so the later part should match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual assumption is that the רישא and סיפא of one ברייתא describe the same kind of situation. If the רישא is after trial, רבה's answer in step 2 becomes hard to hold.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The later part of a teaching

phrases.english: But from the fact that the first clause is where he has stood trial,
the latter clause also is where he has stood trial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the סיפא is before trial.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא and סיפא should be about the same kind of case. The רישא is after trial, so the סיפא is too.

steps.title: Quoting the first part of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the רישא. It includes כפל, ארבעה וחמשה, and the fines of אונס, מפתה and מוציא שם רע in the law of a false oath on money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part teaches: I only know this for things where one pays the basic amount. How do I know that double payment, four and five payment, the rapist, the seducer and the one who spreads a bad name are also included? The verse says "and commits a trespass" to include more.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is bringing the actual text of the רישא, so he can show it must be about after trial. This sets up his proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that a false oath denying these payments also brings the obligation of a קרבן שבועה. The extra word in the פסוק, "ומעלה מעל", widens the rule beyond the basic amount (קרן). The key item for אביי's proof is כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic amount: the value itself
Four or five times payment for stealing and slaughtering or selling a sheep or ox
A man who falsely accuses his new wife

phrases.english: As it teaches in the first clause:
I have only matters
for which one pays the principal.
Double payments, four and five payments,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאוֹנֵס וְהַמְפַתֶּה וּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע, מִנַּיִן —
phrases.english: and the rapist, the seducer, and the defamer: from where do we know?
The verse states: "and commit a trespass," it included more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the text that step 3 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That the רישא is about a case after trial.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The רישא of the ברייתא on a false oath about money (שבועת הפקדון).

steps.title: Double payment only exists after trial
steps.stepSummary: There is no כפל without a trial, so the רישא must be after trial. So the סיפא is after trial too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he had not stood trial, is there double payment at all? So it must be after trial. And since the first part is after trial, the later part is also after trial!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves his point from the mention of כפל in the רישא, and he restates his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief who admits on his own before trial pays no כפל. So a debt of כפל that he could deny exists only after the court ruled. The רישא is therefore after trial, and so the סיפא, where רבי שמעון exempts, is also after trial. That goes against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the case?" Asking for the exact situation

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not quoting the סיפא here. He proves the רישא is after trial and assumes the סיפא matches it.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלֹא עָמַד בַּדִּין, כְּפֵילָא מִי אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: If he has not stood trial, is there double payment?
Rather, it is obvious that it is where he has stood trial.
And from the fact that the first clause is where he has stood trial,
the latter clause also is where he has stood trial!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלֹא עָמַד בַּדִּין, כְּפֵילָא מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the text from step 4 to prove the claim of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Both parts of the ברייתא are about after trial, so רבי שמעון treats a fine as a fine even after trial.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Since כפל only exists after trial, its mention in the רישא proves the setting.

steps.title: רבה: I could split the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה offers a possible answer. The רישא is after trial and the סיפא is before trial, and the whole ברייתא is רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I could answer you that the first part is after trial and the later part is before trial, and the whole thing is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows one way he could escape the challenge, but he is about to say he won't use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, רבי שמעון agrees that after trial a fine becomes money, so he would include כפל in the רישא. He exempts only in the סיפא, which is before trial. That fits רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the whole teaching

phrases.english: He said to him: I could answer you:
the first clause is where he has stood trial,
and the latter clause is where he has not stood trial,
and all of it is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible way out of the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the רישא and סיפא are different situations under one תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both parts must be after trial.
steps.terutzMaskana: Possible but forced. רבה himself sets it aside in the next step.

steps.title: רבה rejects his own forced answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה won't use a forced answer. If the whole ברייתא were רבי שמעון, it should say so.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I won't give you a forced answer. Because if so, you would say to me: let the first part say "רבי שמעון says," or let the later part say "these are the words of רבי שמעון."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why he won't rely on the answer from step 6. This prepares the way for a different answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole ברייתא were רבי שמעון's view, the text would normally name him, either at the start or at the end. Since it doesn't, the split reading is not natural.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach, it should have said

steps.whatToRemember: אביי proved from כפל that the רישא is after trial. רבה could split the ברייתא and give all of it to רבי שמעון, but he rejects that as forced because the text would have named רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: But forced answers I will not answer you.
For if so, you would say to me:
Let the first clause teach: "Rabbi Shimon says,"
or let the latter clause teach: "the words of Rabbi Shimon."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה sets aside his own suggestion from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the answer of step 6 is rejected, not רבה's main rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If the whole ברייתא were רבי שמעון, it would name him at the start or the end, and it doesn't.

steps.title: Both halves are after trial, but by different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the whole ברייתא is after trial. The רישא follows רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the whole ברייתא is about a case where he stood trial. The first part follows the רבנן and the last part follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new answer to אביי. He accepts that both parts of the ברייתא are after trial, but says they come from two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had proven that the רישא is after trial, so the סיפא must be too. רבה agrees that both halves are after trial. He explains the different rulings by saying two different תנאים are speaking: רבנן in the רישא and רבי שמעון in the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the whole ברייתא

phrases.english: Rather: all of it is where he stood trial,
and the first part is the Rabbis, and the last part is Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in Step 7 with a split-authorship reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא between two תנאים (רישא רבנן, סיפא רבי שמעון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed one consistent case and one opinion run through the whole ברייתא, so the סיפא must match the רישא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both halves are after trial. The difference between them is a disagreement between רבנן and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבה agrees there is no קרבן שבועה here
steps.stepSummary: רבה concedes to אביי that the תורה exempts this person from a קרבן שבועה, based on the word 'וכחש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I agree with you about the offering for a false oath: the תורה exempts him, based on the word 'and he denies'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives in on one point. He agrees that a person who falsely swears about this fine does not bring a קרבן שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's word 'וכחש' (he denies) points to a claim that was money from the start. A fine like this did not begin as an ordinary money claim, so the קרבן does not apply. This prepares the next step, where רבה explains what he did mean by 'ממון'.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering brought for falsely swearing about money
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
'And he denies', a word from the פסוק about false oaths

phrases.english: And I agree with you
regarding the offering for an oath
that the Torah exempts him, from 'and he denies'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה narrows his own position by giving in on the קרבן question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no קרבן שבועה for falsely denying this fine, because 'וכחש' requires a claim that was money to begin with.

steps.title: What רבה meant by 'it is money'
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that calling the fine 'ממון' after trial only means the father passes it on to his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when I said it is money, I meant that he passes it on to his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה clarifies his earlier claim. After the trial, the fine counts as ממון only in the sense that the father's heirs inherit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is no longer saying the fine counts as money for a קרבן. He keeps a smaller claim: once there is a court ruling, the payment becomes a normal debt owed to the father, so if he dies, his sons inherit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary money, as opposed to a fine (קְנָס)
To pass it on to his sons as an inheritance

steps.whyThisMatters: This smaller claim is exactly what אביי attacks in the next steps.

phrases.english: And when I said it is money
it was to pass it on to his sons.
phrases.notes: 'His' means the girl's father, who was owed the payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having given up the קרבן point, רבה defines the narrower meaning of 'ממון' he still holds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of a term
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ממון' might have meant ordinary money in every way, including for a קרבן שבועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ממון' only means the payment is inherited by the father's sons.

steps.title: אביי quotes רבי שמעון in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings רבי שמעון's ruling: if the daughter did not collect before the father died, the money is hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: רבי שמעון says that if she did not manage to collect before the father died, the payments belong to her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a source to set up his challenge. Here he only quotes it; the attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון in the משנה, if the father died before the money was collected, the daughter gets it, not the father's heirs. אביי will use this against רבה's claim that the money is inherited.

keyTerms.meaning: Her own, belonging to the daughter herself

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: אביי is the one objecting to רבה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
if she did not manage to collect
before the father died,
they are her own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test רבה's claim from Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that, for רבי שמעון, the fine is inherited by the father's sons
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה that uncollected payments go to the daughter

steps.title: If it is inherited, why does the daughter get it?
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if the money is inherited by the sons, רבי שמעון should give it to the brothers, not to the daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is money in the sense that it passes to his sons, why does it go to her? It should belong to the brothers!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes his challenge. רבה's claim that the money is inherited clashes with רבי שמעון giving it to the daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money were inheritable after trial, the father's death would pass it to his sons, her brothers. Yet רבי שמעון says the daughter keeps it. So it seems רבי שמעון does not treat it as inheritable ממון, which goes against what רבה just said.

keyTerms.meaning: The brothers, the father's sons and heirs

steps.confusionAlert: In this case the brothers are the father's heirs. So 'inherited by his sons' and 'goes to the brothers' are the same thing. That is the whole point of the question.

phrases.english: And if you say it is money
to pass it on to his sons,
why should it be hers?
It should belong to the brothers!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מָמוֹן הָוֵי לְהוֹרִישׁוֹ לְבָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the quote from Step 11 to attack רבה's clarification in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that, for רבי שמעון, the fine after trial is inherited by the father's sons
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inherited money would go to the brothers. רבי שמעון gives it to the daughter, so he cannot hold that it is inherited.

steps.title: רב יוסף's twenty-two-year answer: the father owns it only when it is given
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that רבה and רב יוסף struggled with this question for twenty-two years. When רב יוסף became head of the yeshiva, he answered it: the verse ״וְנָתַן... לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה״ means the father owns the fine only from the moment it is handed to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This question troubled רבה and רב יוסף for twenty-two years without an answer. Then רב יוסף became head of the ישיבה and answered it. The case of the girl is different, because the פסוק says, "And the man who lay with her shall give to the girl's father fifty silver shekels." The תורה gives the money to the father only from the time it is actually given.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's question from Step 12. That question was: why does רבי שמעון give the money to the daughter and not to the brothers? The answer comes from the wording of the פסוק about the אונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says the man "shall give" the money to the father. This teaches that the father owns it only once it is actually handed over. If the father dies before collecting, the money never became his, so it is not part of his estate for his sons to inherit, and it goes to the daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: sat at the head, became head of the yeshiva

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key idea of the whole section: some money belongs to a person only once it reaches his hands, so it cannot be inherited before that.

phrases.english: Rava said: This matter
was difficult for Rabba and Rav Yosef
for twenty-two years, and it was not resolved,

phrases.aramaic: עַד דִּיתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵישָׁא וּפָירְקַהּ:
phrases.english: until Rav Yosef sat at the head and resolved it:
phrases.notes: "Sat at the head" means he became the head of the yeshiva.

phrases.english: There it is different, as the verse says:
"And the man who lay with her shall give
to the girl's father fifty silver shekels,"
the Torah did not give ownership to the father
except from the time of giving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in Step 12 about why the daughter, and not the brothers, gets the money.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from the wording of a פסוק (״וְנָתַן״) that the fine of an אונס is a special case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a fine counts as money after trial and can be inherited, the brothers should get it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fine of an אונס or מפתה belongs to the father only once it is given. If he dies before that, it goes to the daughter.

steps.title: רבה's rule was about other fines
steps.stepSummary: רבה said a fine becomes money that passes to one's sons after trial. That rule was said about other fines, not about the fine of an אונס or מפתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה said a fine becomes money that passes to the father's sons, he meant other fines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fits רבה's earlier statement from Step 10 together with רב יוסף's new answer by limiting how far רבה's rule reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For most קנסות, once the court rules, the payment counts as regular money and can be inherited. The fine for the girl is an exception, because of the word ״וְנָתַן״. So the two ideas do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: to pass it on to his sons as inheritance

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying that the fine for the girl stops being a קנס. He is only saying that the inheritance rule works differently in this one case.

phrases.english: And when Rabba said
"it is money," meaning that he can pass it on to his sons,
that was about other fines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב יוסף's answer to limit רבה's earlier rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a rule so it does not cover this case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's rule seemed to cover every fine, including the fine for the girl.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה's inheritance rule covers other קנסות, but not the fine of an אונס or מפתה.

steps.title: What about the payment for a slave killed by an ox?
steps.stepSummary: The תורה also uses a form of "give" for the thirty shekels paid to a slave's master when an ox kills the slave. Does the master also own that money only once it is given?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, for a slave the פסוק says, "He shall give thirty silver shekels to their master." Would you also say the תורה gives the money to the master only from the time it is given?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's reading of the word "give" by pointing to another verse that uses a similar word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word "give" always means ownership starts only at the moment of payment, the same should be true of the master of a slave. That result seems wrong, so the reading of the פסוק looks too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so, according to your logic

phrases.english: But if so, regarding a slave,
phrases.notes: This is the case of an ox that killed a slave.

phrases.english: where it is written: "Thirty shekels of silver
he shall give to their master,"

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי לֹא זִיכְּתָה תּוֹרָה לָאָדוֹן
phrases.english: so too, did the Torah not give ownership to the master
except from the time of giving?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the way Step 13 read the word "give."
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading of ״וְנָתַן״ in Step 13
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The slave verse also says "give" (״יִתֵּן״). If the word "give" proves that ownership starts only at payment, the master of the slave should follow the same rule, which seems wrong.

steps.title: ״יִתֵּן״ and ״וְנָתַן״ are different words
steps.stepSummary: The two verses use different forms of the word "give," so they do not teach the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״יִתֵּן״ is one thing, and ״וְנָתַן״ is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 15. The exact form of the word matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the form ״וְנָתַן״, used for the girl, teaches that ownership starts at the moment of giving. The slave verse uses ״יִתֵּן״, which does not teach this. So the master owns the payment in the normal way.

keyTerms.meaning: he shall give (the word in the slave verse)
and he shall give (the word in the girl's verse)

phrases.english: "Shall give" (yiten) is separate, and "and he shall give" (venatan) is separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the slave question from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart two similar words in the פסוקים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any verse with the word "give" would teach that ownership starts only at payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ״וְנָתַן״ teaches this. The slave verse's ״יִתֵּן״ does not.

steps.title: Then why did the ברייתא learn it from ״וְכִחֵשׁ״?
steps.stepSummary: If ״וְנָתַן״ is what shows this payment stays a fine, the ברייתא should have learned the exemption from a קרבן שבועה from ״וְנָתַן״, not from ״וְכִחֵשׁ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the ברייתא say "the verse says ״וְכִחֵשׁ״"? It should have said "the verse says ״וְנָתַן״"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer by comparing it with the ברייתא's source for the exemption from a קרבן שבועה, which we saw in Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, ״וְנָתַן״ shows that this payment is still a fine even after trial. If so, that word alone should explain why there is no קרבן שבועה for denying it. The fact that the ברייתא needed ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ suggests it did not read ״וְנָתַן״ this way.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse teaches, the source is

phrases.english: If so, why "the verse says: 'and he denies falsely'"?
It should have said "the verse says: 'and he shall give'"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the reading of ״וְנָתַן״ from Steps 13 and 16, then shows how it clashes with the ברייתא's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ as the source for the exemption from a קרבן שבועה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״וְנָתַן״ already shows the payment stays a fine after trial, the ברייתא should have quoted that word. Quoting ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ instead suggests it did not read ״וְנָתַן״ this way.

steps.title: רבא: ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ is needed when the father inherits from his daughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ is needed for a case where the court already ruled, and then the girl became a בוגרת and died. The father then gets the money as her heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ is needed for a case like this. Her case came to court, then she became an adult and died. In that case, when her father inherits, he is inheriting from her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 17. He shows a case where ״וְנָתַן״ cannot do the job, so the ברייתא needs ״וְכִחֵשׁ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְנָתַן לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה״ only speaks about money the father receives as the girl's father. Here the father is not receiving it as her father. He is inheriting it from her after she grew up and died, so ״וְנָתַן״ does not apply. ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ is still needed, because it frees anyone from a קרבן שבועה when the claim did not start out as normal money.

keyTerms.meaning: her case came before the court and was ruled on
she became a בוגרת, a full adult (past נערה age)

steps.confusionAlert: The father still ends up with the money here. The difference is how he gets it: as an heir, not under ״וְנָתַן לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה״.

phrases.english: Rava said:
When "and deal falsely" was needed —
phrases.notes: This is the ויקרא 5:21 verse about falsely denying a deposit, which brings a קרבן שבועה.

phrases.english: it was for a case where she stood trial,
and then she reached adulthood and died.
For there, when her father inherits —
it is from her that he inherits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17's question of why ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ is needed when ״וְנָתַן״ already exists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״וְנָתַן״ alone covers every case, so ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the father inherits the money from his daughter, ״וְנָתַן״ does not apply, so ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ is needed.

steps.title: In that case the payment is plain money, so why call it a fine?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is after a court ruling, the payment is already normal money. So why does the ברייתא say "excluding these, because they are a קנס"?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can the ברייתא say "excluding these, because they are a fine"? It is regular money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's case using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the court rules, the payment counts as normal money owed (as רבה said in Step 14). But the ברייתא gives the reason for the exemption as "they are a קנס." That wording does not fit a case where the money is no longer a קנס.

keyTerms.meaning: a fine: a fixed payment the Torah sets, not repayment for actual loss

phrases.english: If so,
"excluding these, since they are a fine" —
but it is regular money!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, ״יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁהֵן קְנָס״, מָמוֹן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's case from Step 18 using the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the ברייתא is speaking after a court ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After a ruling the payment is ממון, but the ברייתא calls it קנס.

steps.title: They are excluded because they started out as a fine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the ברייתא as "excluding these, which are originally a קנס."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: read it as "excluding these, which at their root are a fine."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the ברייתא's wording so that it fits רבא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not saying the payment is still a קנס now. It means the claim began as a קנס. ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ only makes a person liable when the claim started out as normal money, like a deposit.

keyTerms.meaning: their origin, what they were at the start

steps.whatToRemember: ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ looks at where a claim started. A payment that began as a קנס stays outside the קרבן שבועה even after a court turns it into money owed.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
"Excluding these, whose origin is a fine."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: יָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ שֶׁעִיקָּרָן קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "They are a קנס" means the payment is a fine right now.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the payment began as a קנס.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי שמעון in the משנה in שבועות
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון exempts because "one does not pay a קנס on his own admission." That suggests that after a court ruling he would pay on his own word, and then he would owe a קרבן שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: "רבי שמעון exempts, because one does not pay a fine on his own admission." So the reason is that he did not stand trial. But if he did stand trial, he pays on his own admission, and he should also owe a קרבן שבועה!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's idea that ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ exempts even after a court ruling. He uses an inference from רבי שמעון's words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's stated reason is that a קנס is not paid on one's own admission. That reason only works before a court ruling. After a ruling, a person who admits must pay, so by that reason he should owe a קרבן שבועה. This contradicts רבה's reading in Steps 8–9 that רבי שמעון exempts even after trial because of ״וְכִחֵשׁ״. Steps 18–20 rested on that same reading.

keyTerms.meaning: the offering for a false oath denying money owed

phrases.english: He raised an objection:
phrases.notes: אביי is challenging רבה again, this time about how רבה reads רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts him,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם קְנָס עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: since one does not pay a fine on his own admission.
The reason is that he did not stand trial;

phrases.aramaic: הָא עָמַד בַּדִּין, דִּמְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: but if he stood trial, so that he does pay on his own admission,
he should be liable to a קרבן שבועה as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן פּוֹטֵר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם קְנָס עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Steps 18–20 that he is exempt even after a court ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reading that רבי שמעון (the סיפא of the ברייתא, Steps 8–9) exempts from a קרבן שבועה even after he stood trial, because of ״וְכִחֵשׁ״. Steps 18 and 20 build on this.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's stated reason only covers the time before a ruling. That suggests he would be liable after one.

steps.title: רבי שמעון was arguing with the רבנן on their own terms
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that ״וְכִחֵשׁ״ exempts even after a court ruling. He gave the "own admission" reason only to win at least part of the point using the רבנן's own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון was speaking to the רבנן according to their view: "In my view, even after he stood trial, the תורה exempts him because of ״וְכִחֵשׁ״. But in your view, at least agree with me where he did not stand trial, that when the claimant claims, he is claiming a fine..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The reason quoted in the משנה is not רבי שמעון's full view; it is an argument he made to the רבנן. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון himself exempts in every case, because of ״וְכִחֵשׁ״, since the claim began as a קנס. The רבנן do not accept that. So he argues with them using their own view: "Before a ruling, the claim is clearly a קנס, so at least agree with me there." The inference from his words therefore says nothing about his own opinion after a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: according to their words, using the other side's own view

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common way to answer a question in the גמרא. A sage's stated reason may only be an argument aimed at the other side, not his full opinion.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon was speaking to them according to the words of the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּעָמַד בַּדִּין —
phrases.english: "According to me, even though he stood trial —
the Merciful One exempts him from 'and deal falsely.'
But according to you,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹדוֹ לִי מִיהַת הֵיכָא דְּלֹא עָמַד בַּדִּין,
phrases.english: at least agree with me where he did not stand trial,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי קָא תָּבַע, קְנָסָא קָא תָּבַע,
phrases.english: that when one claims, it is a fine that he claims,
phrases.notes: His sentence isn't finished yet; it keeps going on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument according to the opponent's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's stated reason shows that he would make the man liable after a court ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון exempts even after a ruling because of ״וְכִחֵשׁ״. His stated reason was only aimed at the רבנן's view.
